reader.notes: One edition-free min/max test (RecordLengthConflicts) for every organization; NoteRecordRead caps the delivered length at the VARYING maximum so the DEPENDING item and INTO sender see the truncated record. A fixed-length record-sequential file carries no length on the medium, so only its partial final record can be a short record (DOC-A.1-146, implementor latitude).

refuter.evidence: r2gr13.cob (refute-1985-124/r2gr13-001, --std 85): FW (RECORD IS VARYING 1 TO 20 DEPENDING DW, 01 X(20)) writes records of 3, 15 and 8 characters to r2.dat (each 00); FR on the same file (RECORD IS VARYING FROM 2 TO 20 DEPENDING DR, record descriptions 01 R6 X(6) and 01 R10 X(10), legal by §1985:VII.3.8.3 SR2) reads them INTO T20. Printed: R1 00 03 [ABC...]; R2 00 15 [ABCDEFGHIJ          ] [ABCDEFGHIJ]; R3 00 08. The 15-character record exceeds the maximum size specified by the record description entries (10): the runtime DID truncate it to 10 (characters KLMNO are gone from the record area and from the INTO move) but set I-O status 00, not the record length conflict 04, and left DR = 15 though only 10 characters are in the area. The 3-character record is shorter than the smallest record description (6) and also reads 00. Cause: FileConnector#RecordLengthConflicts tests VaryMin/VaryMax, which FileModel#VaryMin/VaryMax take from the stated integer-2/integer-3, not the record description entries GR13 names. Same output at --std 2023 (r2gr13-002), so cause b. No kb/Work note found (grep of kb/Work for the GR13 wording, VaryMax, integer-3: PB5480 is the keyed zero-byte case, PB2519 report files). cite.py: OK  §1985:VII.4.4.4 GR13 (4.4.4 General Rules) the text is in GR13 ('the record is truncated on the right to the maximum size'); OK  §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR12; OK  §1985:VII.1.3.5 ... GRL2.1b.
refuter.corrected: PARTIAL (wrong-answer, silent; cause b): a READ of a record longer than the largest record description of file-name-1 but within integer-3 is truncated to that maximum with status 00 instead of 04, and the DEPENDING item reports the untruncated length; a record shorter than the smallest record description but at least integer-2 reads 00. GR13 bounds the conflict by 'the record description entries for file-name-1'. The short leg alone rests on a reading (§1985:VII.1.3.5 words 04 against the fixed file attributes, which integer-2 sets), but the long leg is wrong on either reading: the record was truncated, which GR13 pairs with the 04, or it should not have been truncated at all.

adjudication.reason: The mechanism of kb/Work PB5785 in its `RECORD IS VARYING ... DEPENDING ON` form: status 00, the DEPENDING item says 15, and READ INTO moves 10 characters. By the ruling beside PB5785 the RECORD clause sizes the move, here through the item it names: 15 characters.
